accept.why: Figma has 13px Regular uppercase with no icon; .pf-button is 13px SemiBold sentence case. Using the library component beats matching the product file.

peoplePerCard.comment: Two avatars: one in the header's subject field, one on the single stage card. The dashed add-card carries none.

placeholders.comment: EMPTY, deliberately. Every string on this page is Figma's own, so there is nothing to declare and the whole screen is held to Figma's exact words. See `portraits` for why one avatar shows a monogram.

portraits.comment: Figma's People instances are sample content dropped in without matching the text. This screen takes the TEXT as authoritative and binds a portrait only where a People variant of that name exists.

observations.comment: Things the design says that disagree with each other. Reproduced exactly rather than reconciled, because picking whichever two look consistent would be inventing a decision.
observations.stageCardSignals: Card 16157:22041 is styled as the THEME card (background/theme fill, 1px border/theme stroke) and carries an IN PROGRESS stepper, yet its tag reads COMPLETE in green. Three signals, three different states. The sibling screens show white+Done+Complete and theme+In progress+In-progress; this is a third combination.

divergences.comment: Known, deliberate differences from Figma. Listed so they are decisions rather than drift.
divergences.components: Stepper, People, Rectangle Tags and Right arrow come from a non-People-First library (F-018).
divergences.tags: Figma uses Rectangle Tags with alpha fills. The prototype uses the People First Tags component.
divergences.personName12px: 12px is not on the People First type ramp. Recorded as a gap; the prototype uses the 13px label class with a declared `accept`.
divergences.buttonCase: Figma draws Close case 13px Regular UPPERCASE with no icon; .pf-button is 13px SemiBold sentence case. The library component wins, so the page reads 'Close case', not 'CLOSE CASE'.
divergences.cardsAreLocalCss: The header and subject are plain Figma FRAMES, and the stage card is `Clickable card` from a non-People-First library. None is the People First Card, so they are built in local CSS to Figma's measured values and asserted by the `frame` block above. `.pf-card` used to stand in for them at radius 8 / padding 20, which made every screen about a fifth taller than the design.

frame.name: subject field 16299:9443 — 217 wide, no gap between the two

frame_comment: Machine-readable geometry, read by scripts/verify-frame.mjs. Every value is from the saved extract in dsskill/runs/. These frames are NOT the People First Card: the header and subject are plain Figma frames (page layout), and the stage card is `Clickable card` from a non-People-First library (F-018). They are built in local CSS as declared GAPs — and this block is what makes that checkable rather than merely declared.
